intended_object: A Boolean-style tag on the library's own `RuleApp` inductive type: it says whether a rule application in the split sequent calculus for GL uses one of the two box (modal) rules, `boxₗ` or `boxᵣ`. I inferred this from the docstring ("Auxiliary declaration"), the definition's name and how the library uses it (`nbEdge`, `exists_box_on_loop`, …).
explanation:
The definition holds exactly on the constructors `boxₗ` and `boxᵣ` of the local `RuleApp` type and fails on all the others. `true`/`false` are coerced to `Prop`, so this is just a case split on constructors. It works correctly as that tag. The library uses it to state that edges which are not box edges shrink the sequent, and that every loop in a proof graph contains a box rule.

This is not a standard mathematical notion. It is a technical classifier on the library's own syntax of rule applications, used as a tool inside its proofs, and Mathlib has nothing comparable to measure it against. The docstring itself calls it an "Auxiliary declaration".
